name: Stanley Lifestyles Ltd
title: Stanley Lifestyles Ltd - 544202 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Stanley Lifestyles FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5%, but Q4 revenue fell on B2B export pull-down and management guides only conservative FY27 growth.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year spent acquiring franchise markets (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune) into company-owned stores and consolidating subsidiaries into one listed entity. Q4 FY26 saw a decline in B2B demand from mid-Q4, with roughly Rs. 15 crore of B2B revenue pulled down due to West Asia conflict disruptions to a large export client. Gross margin for FY26 improved to 57.5% from 56.3%, while cash was about Rs. 200 crore versus Rs. 215 crore a year earlier despite capex above Rs. 60 crore. Management opened 11 stores and closed three over 12 months, and guided to aspirational double-digit growth but a conservative stance for FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of FY27
Higher depreciation and finance cost (lease front-loading under Ind AS)

financial_highlights.value: about 4% for mature stores (over 3 years); Stanley Level Next +11.6%, Sofas & More +3.5%, Stanley Boutique -8.1%

financial_highlights.change: as franchise markets were converted to COCO

segments.name: B2C (retail, COCO and FOFO)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q4 FY26 revenue; roughly 75% of B2C business is driven by confirmed customer orders. Store network is 49 COCO and 22 FOFO stores, with 33 stores under 3 years and 38 over 3 years.

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: About 30% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Around Rs. 15 crore pulled down in Q4 due to delays from West Asia conflict on exports to a large global furniture brand; management expects recovery around Q2 FY27 and is targeting high-end B2B and some exports.

guidance_outlook: Management is aspirational about double-digit growth in FY27 but says it will be very conservative given global conditions, prioritising profitability and cash.
B2C and B2B supply chain and export disruptions expected to flow into FY27; B2B export recovery hoped for by Q2 FY27.
QCO regulation on furniture imports effective 15 August 2026, expected to deter imports, the main competition.
Flagship 60,000+ sq ft Hyderabad store (Stanley Superlative Living) now scheduled to go live around July 2026 after regulatory delays.
Sri Lanka first store (Sofas & More brand, pilot with Singer Group) to open at start of Q2 FY27, with possible expansion to five or six shop-in-shops.
Management expects handovers in top six cities to accelerate and peak in FY28 and FY29; new digital platform and revamped website targeted by end FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex in FY26 exceeded Rs. 60 crore, the highest ever; management says investment will continue for some time while consolidating mature markets.
Opened 11 new stores and shut three underperforming stores in the last 12 months; five additional stores expected to commence operations shortly.
Over half of stores are still in gestation/ramp-up; ROI on a store is about 3 years (15-18 months in some catchments, 24-36 months in Bangalore micro-markets).
Three to four legacy stores to be relocated or consolidated into larger formats; consolidation to be completed by end FY27; store count may fall.
Around 85-90% of store furniture is now made in India versus about 70% three to four years ago; delivery in 6-8 weeks versus 4-5 months for imports.
demand_pricing: Mature stores over three years grew about 4% annually over the last four years; management expects 10-15% going forward as kitchen and cabinetry is added.
Project handovers across top six cities are delayed; footfalls are steady but conversion cycles longer.
Competition mainly from import traders (Europe, Turkey, China high-end); local manufacturer-designers are secondary; low-end B2B is not targeted due to unorganised competition.
Gross margin supported by best-cost country sourcing; USD and EUR appreciation raised input costs.
Marketing spend has historically stayed below 10% of revenue; management plans to increase event and fair participation (AD, ELLE Decor) and possibly social media influencers from 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth of stores open over three years and why company-owned store revenue looks flat since 2023 despite more stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Mature stores have grown about 4% a year; the flat revenue reflects a 35% drop in franchisee business and about Rs. 18-20 crore lost from leather trading moved to cash-and-carry, plus Rs. 24 crore cited in total.

qa_highlights.question: What were the short-term disruptions in the last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A large global furniture brand's B2B exports to the Middle East were halted by the war-related logistics standstill; orders were postponed and recovery is expected by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue low-end B2B inquiries given low plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its back-end is built for premium B2C and it cannot compete with unorganised low-end B2B; it is pursuing high-end B2B inquiries from MNCs and considering exports.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics and when stores start generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says ROI, including interest on capex, is about 3 years; some catchments take 15-18 months and Bangalore micro-markets 24-36 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to raw material delays due to the US-Iran war and about Rs. 15 crore B2B revenue pull-down; it said full-year gross margin improved and B2C margins are secure.

qa_highlights.question: Digital discovery, website and pricing policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted it has been slow on digital, said SAP is implemented, and promised a new AI-assisted website, with AR/VR tools, by end FY27.

risks_watch: Q4 FY26 revenue decline and continued B2B export disruption from West Asia conflict; management expects recovery only from Q2 FY27.
Franchisee business down 35%, and conversion of franchise markets to COCO adds capex and lease-related depreciation and finance cost.
Store ramp-up: over half of stores are immature and 3-year ROI is management's own metric; watch for store closures and relocations.
Subsidiary merger into a single listed entity, with the Rs. 3.3 crore labour code exceptional charge and KMP compensation overlap.
Effectiveness of QCO from 15 August 2026 in curbing imports, and Hyderabad flagship going live around July 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident about long-term positioning and the debt-free balance sheet, but cautious and defensive on near-term top-line growth, with management repeatedly attributing weakness to external factors. Answers on digital capability, pricing and the franchise-to-COCO transition were candid about past slowness but light on hard numbers.
key_quotes: We are not building Stanley for the next quarter; we are building Stanley for the next decade.
In the luxury segment, scale without control leads to dilution. We have consciously chosen control.
So, we are very prudent in our investment.

While we are quite aspirational to deliver definitely double-digit growth, I hope that in terms of how the global situation is, we are reserving ourselves and I would say we will be very conservative.

growth.why: Management is aspirational about double-digit FY27 growth but gives no number and calls its stance very conservative; backing is partial, with a Hyderabad store going live around July 2026, five stores starting shortly, an order book of about Rs 62 crore, and B2B export recovery hoped for by Q2 FY27.
